summary: vite-vue-path-map injects obfuscated license kill-switch and beacon into built bundles
details: Package advertises itself as a Vite plugin that generates a Vue file-path/component-name map. During Rollup's generateBundle hook, it reads global['gva-project-name'] and global['gva-secret'], performs an authorization hash check, and on failure splices a base64-obfuscated payload into a randomly selected non-entry JS chunk at a randomized AST insertion point. When the installer's built application is loaded in a browser on a non-localhost hostname, the injected snippet decodes an atob-wrapped URL to plugin.gin-vue-admin.com/api/shopImage/view (fetched as an invisible image) and overwrites the DOM via document.write with a Chinese '项目未授权' (project unauthorized) page. The beacon URL, image CSS, and unauthorized-page HTML are stored as base64 literals and decoded only at runtime. None of this behavior is documented in the README, which describes only path-map generation. The consequence for anyone who installs this plugin is that their production bundle silently carries an undisclosed, obfuscated kill-switch and third-party beacon that fires on their end users' browsers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
